title: Fābella · Rūfus et cāseus (× 3)
summary: Iulia's Saturday: rain, coffee, her dog Rufus, the market, and a stolen cheese. English then Latin, free voices, Latin read from IPA. Quotes: Canis timidus vehementius lātrat quam mordet (Quintus Curtius), Post nūbila Phoebus (old saying). Played 3 times. Latin v said as v.
pairs: Today I'll tell you all about my Saturday.
Hodiē vōbīs dē diē Sāturnī meō nārrābō.
On Saturday I got up late.
I drank coffee in the kitchen.
Only one coffee. Not too much.
Then I looked out of the window.
My dog was looking at me.
I didn't want to walk in the rain.
At the market there were many people.
I shouted too: Rufus, come back!
But Rufus did not come back.
He grabbed a big piece of cheese.
I walked through the market. Where was Rufus?
Per forum ambulāvī. Ubi erat Rūfus?
He was sitting under a table.
He was happy. I was not happy.
Ille laetus erat. Ego nōn laeta eram.
A man was laughing. It was my friend Marcus.
Vir rīdēbat. Erat amīcus meus Marcus.
Marcus said: your dog is a thief!
Marcus dīxit: canis tuus fūr est!
I said: yes. But a friendly thief.
I said: no. He barks, but he doesn't bite.
Dīxī: minimē. Lātrat, sed nōn mordet.
Quintus Curtius wrote: a timid dog barks more than it bites.
Quīntus Curtius scrīpsit: canis timidus vehementius lātrat quam mordet.
That is: people who shout loudly are often afraid.
Id est: quī valdē clāmant, saepe timent.
Marcus said: after the clouds, the sun!
It's an old saying. Phoebus is the god of the sun.
Vetus dictum est. Phoebus deus sōlis est.
That is: after bad times, good times come.
Id est: post tempora mala veniunt tempora bona.
We walked home together in the sun.
At home I read a book.
He was dreaming about cheese, I think.
